what: A dial that turns a one-screen stage with wheel, drag and arrow keys to pick items one at a time. The wheel adds (deltaY ÷ screen height .8) steps to the target, and a drag moves one step per screen width. The visible value follows the target with damp(7) (28 while dragging), the release velocity decays as exp(−7.5t), and starting .35 seconds after release it snaps to the nearest step with damp(2.5). Each item gets --fx-offset (item − position), which the consuming css lays out as a cylinder, strip or overlap, and the center item gets aria-current.
ease: damp(7) follows · damp(2.5) sticks · exp(−7.5t) inertia

options.per: Screen heights needed to advance one notch with the wheel, default 0.8
options.drag: Number of cells to advance when dragging one screen width, default 1
options.follow: Strength at which the shown value follows the target (damp), default 7
options.snap: Strength of snapping to the nearest cell (damp), default 2.5 — 0 means no snapping
options.delay: Seconds from release until snapping begins, default 0.35
options.loop: If false, stops at the start and end (default loops endlessly)
options.[data-fx-part=item]: Items to choose from. Each receives --fx-offset, and the middle one gets aria-current="true"
options.--fx-pos: Current position on an element (fractional, per item) — for what CSS cannot do, like 3D scenes, listen to the fx:dial event (detail.pos·index)

note: Because it intercepts the wheel (preventDefault), attach it only to a single-screen stage — intercept only while the cursor is over the element, and on phones accept only horizontal dragging so vertical swipes scroll the page (touch-action: pan-y)
